title: How Indians can invest in US stocks
hook: Three routes, and how they differ.
slides: 1. Your Indian broker (GIFT City)
Several Indian brokers now offer US stocks through GIFT City (IFSC). You use the same app you already know.
2. A foreign broker under LRS
Open an account with an overseas or Indian-partnered platform and remit money under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme.
3. Indian mutual funds & ETFs
International funds and ETFs give US exposure in rupees. Many international funds pause new money when industry overseas limits are reached.
Compare before you choose
Look at FX conversion costs, brokerage, custody fees, minimums and how tax reporting works for each route.
takeaway: Pick the route on costs, convenience and tax reporting, not just on which app is easiest.

title: LRS in plain English
hook: The rule behind every rupee you send abroad.
slides: What it is
The RBI's Liberalised Remittance Scheme lets resident individuals send money abroad for permitted purposes, including investing.
The limit
Up to USD 2,50,000 per person per financial year, across all LRS purposes combined.
TCS
Banks collect tax at source (TCS) on larger remittances. It is not an extra tax: you can adjust it against your income tax or claim it back.
Check current rules
Thresholds and TCS rates change in Budgets. Confirm the latest numbers with your bank or tax adviser before remitting.
takeaway: LRS sets how much you can send; TCS is a prepaid tax you can adjust, not a cost.

title: How US stock gains are taxed in India
hook: Two kinds of income, two sets of rules.
slides: Dividends
US companies withhold tax on dividends paid to Indian residents. The dividend is also taxable in India; the US tax can be claimed as a credit (Form 67).
Capital gains
US shares are treated as unlisted foreign assets in India: the holding period for long-term treatment is longer than for Indian listed shares.
Report everything
Foreign holdings must be disclosed in your ITR's foreign assets schedule (Schedule FA), even if you made no gains.
Get it right
Tax rules change often. A chartered accountant who handles foreign income is worth it.
takeaway: Plan for dividend credit, the longer holding period and Schedule FA reporting.

title: The rupee effect
hook: Why US returns often look better in rupees.
slides: Two returns in one
Your rupee return = the US asset's return in dollars + the change in USD/INR.
When the rupee weakens
If the rupee falls against the dollar, your US investments are worth more in rupees, adding to returns.
It works both ways
If the rupee strengthens, it reduces your rupee returns, even if the US asset rose.
A natural hedge
Many Indian goals have dollar-linked costs: foreign education, travel, imported goods. US assets can help offset that.
takeaway: Currency is part of the return. Treat it as a feature, not a guarantee.

title: Why diversify beyond India?
slides: Different leaders
Many of the world's largest companies in technology, healthcare and consumer brands are listed in the US, not India.
Different cycles
Indian and US markets don't always rise and fall together, which can smooth a portfolio's ride.
Concentration risk
Your job, home and savings are usually all tied to India's economy. Global exposure spreads that risk.
How much?
There's no single answer. Many investors hold a modest slice abroad and rebalance it yearly.
takeaway: Global diversification is about resilience, not chasing the hottest market.

title: US estate tax: the hidden risk
hook: A rule many Indian investors don't know.
slides: What it is
The US can levy estate tax on US assets held by non-residents when they pass away.
A low threshold
For non-residents, the exemption is very small compared with what US citizens get, so even modest portfolios can be affected.
Why it matters
Your heirs may need to deal with US paperwork and tax before they can access the money.
Ways investors manage it
Some use funds domiciled outside the US or Indian fund routes. Discuss your situation with a tax professional.
takeaway: Before building a large US portfolio, understand estate tax and plan for it.
